name: wait_event_interruptible_locked
prose: Function-like macro (an expression of type int). It evaluates condition once first and yields 0 without sleeping if it is true; otherwise it yields __wait_event_interruptible_locked(wq, condition, 0, do_wait_intr). That loop declares a wait entry with DEFINE_WAIT, and repeats: call do_wait_intr(&wq, &wait), stop if it returns nonzero, else stop when condition is true. do_wait_intr adds the entry to the tail of the waitqueue if not already queued, sets TASK_INTERRUPTIBLE, returns -ERESTARTSYS if a signal is pending, and otherwise releases the lock with spin_unlock(&wq->lock), calls schedule(), retakes it with spin_lock(&wq->lock) and returns 0. After the loop it removes the entry from the queue, sets the task state to TASK_RUNNING and yields the loop's value. So the value is 0 when condition was seen true and -ERESTARTSYS when a signal was pending while condition was false. The caller must hold wq.lock (taken the matching way) on entry; condition is evaluated with the lock held and the lock is held again when the macro finishes. wq is the waitqueue head object, not a pointer.
note: Checked against __wait_event_interruptible_locked (wait.h:779-793) and do_wait_intr / do_wait_intr_irq (kernel/sched/wait.c:333-365). Macro; the earlier contracts were prose and are dropped.

name: wait_event_interruptible_locked_irq
prose: Function-like macro (an expression of type int). It evaluates condition once first and yields 0 without sleeping if it is true; otherwise it yields __wait_event_interruptible_locked(wq, condition, 0, do_wait_intr_irq). That loop declares a wait entry with DEFINE_WAIT, and repeats: call do_wait_intr_irq(&wq, &wait), stop if it returns nonzero, else stop when condition is true. do_wait_intr_irq adds the entry to the tail of the waitqueue if not already queued, sets TASK_INTERRUPTIBLE, returns -ERESTARTSYS if a signal is pending, and otherwise releases the lock with spin_unlock_irq(&wq->lock), calls schedule(), retakes it with spin_lock_irq(&wq->lock) and returns 0. After the loop it removes the entry from the queue, sets the task state to TASK_RUNNING and yields the loop's value. So the value is 0 when condition was seen true and -ERESTARTSYS when a signal was pending while condition was false. The caller must hold wq.lock (taken the matching way) on entry; condition is evaluated with the lock held and the lock is held again when the macro finishes. Because spin_unlock_irq enables interrupts around the sleep, the caller must be in a context where that is allowed.
note: Checked against __wait_event_interruptible_locked (wait.h:779-793) and do_wait_intr / do_wait_intr_irq (kernel/sched/wait.c:333-365). Macro; the earlier contracts were prose and are dropped.

name: wait_event_interruptible_exclusive_locked
prose: Function-like macro (an expression of type int). It evaluates condition once first and yields 0 without sleeping if it is true; otherwise it yields __wait_event_interruptible_locked(wq, condition, 1, do_wait_intr). That loop declares a wait entry with DEFINE_WAIT, sets WQ_FLAG_EXCLUSIVE on it, and repeats: call do_wait_intr(&wq, &wait), stop if it returns nonzero, else stop when condition is true. do_wait_intr adds the entry to the tail of the waitqueue if not already queued, sets TASK_INTERRUPTIBLE, returns -ERESTARTSYS if a signal is pending, and otherwise releases the lock with spin_unlock(&wq->lock), calls schedule(), retakes it with spin_lock(&wq->lock) and returns 0. After the loop it removes the entry from the queue, sets the task state to TASK_RUNNING and yields the loop's value. So the value is 0 when condition was seen true and -ERESTARTSYS when a signal was pending while condition was false. The caller must hold wq.lock (taken the matching way) on entry; condition is evaluated with the lock held and the lock is held again when the macro finishes. Being exclusive means a wake-up walking the queue stops after waking this entry (documented in the header comment).
note: Checked against __wait_event_interruptible_locked (wait.h:779-793) and do_wait_intr / do_wait_intr_irq (kernel/sched/wait.c:333-365). Macro; the earlier contracts were prose and are dropped.

name: wait_event_interruptible_exclusive_locked_irq
prose: Function-like macro (an expression of type int). It evaluates condition once first and yields 0 without sleeping if it is true; otherwise it yields __wait_event_interruptible_locked(wq, condition, 1, do_wait_intr_irq). That loop declares a wait entry with DEFINE_WAIT, sets WQ_FLAG_EXCLUSIVE on it, and repeats: call do_wait_intr_irq(&wq, &wait), stop if it returns nonzero, else stop when condition is true. do_wait_intr_irq adds the entry to the tail of the waitqueue if not already queued, sets TASK_INTERRUPTIBLE, returns -ERESTARTSYS if a signal is pending, and otherwise releases the lock with spin_unlock_irq(&wq->lock), calls schedule(), retakes it with spin_lock_irq(&wq->lock) and returns 0. After the loop it removes the entry from the queue, sets the task state to TASK_RUNNING and yields the loop's value. So the value is 0 when condition was seen true and -ERESTARTSYS when a signal was pending while condition was false. The caller must hold wq.lock (taken the matching way) on entry; condition is evaluated with the lock held and the lock is held again when the macro finishes. Because spin_unlock_irq enables interrupts around the sleep, the caller must be in a context where that is allowed. Being exclusive means a wake-up walking the queue stops after waking this entry (documented in the header comment).
note: Checked against __wait_event_interruptible_locked (wait.h:779-793) and do_wait_intr / do_wait_intr_irq (kernel/sched/wait.c:333-365). Macro; the earlier contracts were prose and are dropped.

name: wait_event_killable
prose: Function-like macro, a GNU statement expression of type int. It calls might_sleep(), then if !(condition) it runs ___wait_event(wq_head, condition, TASK_KILLABLE, 0, 0, schedule()), which repeatedly queues the task, sleeps in TASK_KILLABLE until woken, and re-tests condition each time; it yields 0 once condition is seen true and -ERESTARTSYS if prepare_to_wait_event reports that a fatal signal is pending while condition is false. If condition is true at the start it yields 0 without sleeping. The result is stored in an int. condition is expanded more than once. The task is dequeued (finish_wait) on the normal exit; wake_up must be called by whoever changes the condition.
note: Checked against ___wait_event (wait.h:302-327) and prepare_to_wait_event (kernel/sched/wait.c:290). Macro; earlier contract was prose and is dropped.

name: wait_event_state
prose: Function-like macro, a GNU statement expression of type int. It calls might_sleep(), then if !(condition) it runs ___wait_event(wq_head, condition, state, 0, 0, schedule()), sleeping in the task state given by state and re-testing condition on each wake-up. It yields 0 once condition is seen true (also immediately if it is true at the start) and -ERESTARTSYS if the state is one a signal can interrupt (a non-constant state is always treated as possibly interruptible) and prepare_to_wait_event reports a pending signal for that state while condition is false. condition is expanded more than once.
note: Checked against ___wait_event (wait.h:302-327), ___wait_is_interruptible (wait.h:284). Macro; contract dropped.

name: wait_event_state_exclusive
prose: Function-like macro, a GNU statement expression of type int, the same as wait_event_state except the wait entry is queued with WQ_FLAG_EXCLUSIVE (exclusive argument 1 of ___wait_event): after might_sleep(), if !(condition) it runs ___wait_event(wq_head, condition, state, 1, 0, schedule()). It yields 0 once condition is seen true and -ERESTARTSYS if a signal that is able to interrupt the given state is pending while condition is false. Exclusive means a wake-up walking the queue stops after waking this entry.
note: Checked against ___wait_event; the exclusive flag only changes how the entry is queued and woken. Macro; contract dropped.

name: wait_event_lock_irq_cmd
prose: Function-like macro (a do { } while (0) statement, no value). If condition is already true it does nothing. Otherwise it runs ___wait_event(wq_head, condition, TASK_UNINTERRUPTIBLE, 0, 0, ...), whose wait step is spin_unlock_irq(&lock); cmd; schedule(); spin_lock_irq(&lock). It therefore returns only when condition is true (uninterruptible, so no signal exit). The caller must hold lock on entry; it is held on return, and is released, with interrupts enabled, while cmd runs and the task sleeps. condition is tested with the lock held (and after every wake-up).
note: Checked against __wait_event_lock_irq (wait.h:226-231). Macro; contract was prose, dropped.

name: xz_crc32
note: Only a declaration in this header (uint32_t xz_crc32(const uint8_t *buf, size_t size, uint32_t crc); inside #if XZ_INTERNAL_CRC32); there is no body in the slice, so nothing to describe here.

name: __FP_FRAC_SRS_1
prose: Function-like macro that assigns to X (so X must be an lvalue, and is evaluated several times) and yields the assigned value: X = (X >> N) | sticky. sticky is (X & 1) when N is a compile-time constant equal to 1, and otherwise ((X << (_FP_W_TYPE_SIZE - N)) != 0), i.e. 1 if any of the N bits shifted out of X was set and 0 if not. The sz argument is not used. Meaningful only for 0 < N < _FP_W_TYPE_SIZE; a shift by the full word width or more is not defined by this macro.
note: Macro; contract was prose, dropped. Precedence: the sticky ternary is parenthesised, the shift binds tighter than |.

name: _FP_FRAC_SLL_1
prose: Function-like macro (do { } while (0), no value) that shifts the one-word fraction X_f (token-pasted from X) left: if N is a compile-time constant equal to 1 it does X_f += X_f, otherwise X_f <<= N. Bits shifted out of the word are lost; N is expected to be less than the word size.
note: Macro; contract dropped.

name: _FP_MUL_MEAT_1_imm
prose: Function-like macro (do { } while (0), no value). It sets R_f = X_f * Y_f as a single word multiply (truncated to the word size, so correct only if the host word is at least twice the fraction width, as the header comment assumes) and then applies _FP_FRAC_SRS_1(R, wfracbits - 1, 2 * wfracbits), a right shift of R_f by wfracbits - 1 that ORs a sticky bit for any shifted-out bits. It modifies R_f only.
note: Macro; contract dropped.

name: _FP_MUL_MEAT_1_hard
prose: Function-like macro (do { } while (0), no value) that multiplies the one-word fractions X_f and Y_f into a two-word product using half-word pieces: it splits each into high and low halves of _FP_W_TYPE_SIZE/2 bits, forms the four partial products, adds the two cross products (adding a carry of 1 << (word/2) into the high word if that sum wraps), splits the cross sum across the two words and adds it to the low-by-low and high-by-high products with _FP_FRAC_ADD_2. It then applies _FP_FRAC_SRS_2(_z, wfracbits - 1, 2 * wfracbits), a sticky right shift of the two-word product, and sets R_f = _z_f0, the low word. Its locals _xh, _xl, _yh, _yl, _z_f0, _z_f1, _a_f0, _a_f1 are declared inside the block.
note: Old prose said '16-bit-half partial products'; the code uses half-words of _FP_W_TYPE_SIZE/2 bits. Macro; contract dropped.

name: _FP_DIV_MEAT_1_udiv
prose: Function-like macro (do { } while (0), no value) that divides one-word fractions using the udiv_qrnnd double-word primitive. If X_f < Y_f it decrements R_e and forms the dividend nh:nl = (X_f >> _FP_WFRACXBITS_fs) : (X_f << _FP_WFRACBITS_fs); otherwise nh:nl = (X_f >> (_FP_WFRACXBITS_fs + 1)) : (X_f << (_FP_WFRACBITS_fs - 1)). It calls udiv_qrnnd(_q, _r, _nh, _nl, Y_f) and sets R_f = _q | (_r != 0), the quotient with the low bit set as sticky when the remainder is nonzero. X_f is left unchanged; R_e may change. There is no test for Y_f being zero here.
note: Macro; contract was prose, dropped.

name: _FP_SQRT_MEAT_1
prose: Function-like macro (do { } while (0), no value) implementing a bit-at-a-time square root on one-word fractions. While q != _FP_WORK_ROUND it sets T_f = S_f + q; if T_f <= X_f it sets S_f = T_f + q, X_f -= T_f and R_f += q; then it shifts X left by one (_FP_FRAC_SLL_1) and halves q. When the loop ends, if X_f is nonzero it sets the _FP_WORK_ROUND bit of R_f if S_f < X_f and always sets the _FP_WORK_STICKY bit of R_f. So R_f accumulates the root bits and the round and sticky bits report an inexact result. The loop ends only if q reaches exactly _FP_WORK_ROUND by repeated halving; q, X, S, T and R are all modified.
note: Macro; contract was prose and the 'floor of the square root' claim was imprecise (R_f carries extra round/sticky bits); rewritten from the body.

name: _FP_FRAC_GE_1
prose: Function-like macro: expands to (X##_f >= Y##_f), a comparison of the one-word fractions X_f and Y_f as _FP_W_TYPE values, yielding 1 if X_f is at least Y_f and 0 otherwise. X and Y are names that are pasted with _f, not general expressions; nothing is modified.
note: Macro; contract dropped.

name: _FP_SQRT_MEAT_2
prose: Function-like macro (do { } while (0), no value) implementing a bit-at-a-time square root on two-word fractions (words f1 high, f0 low). Loop 1, while q is nonzero: T_f1 = S_f1 + q; if T_f1 <= X_f1 then S_f1 = T_f1 + q, X_f1 -= T_f1, R_f1 += q; then _FP_FRAC_SLL_2(X, 1) and q >>= 1. It then reloads q with the top bit of a word. Loop 2, while q != _FP_WORK_ROUND: T_f0 = S_f0 + q, T_f1 = S_f1; if T <= X as a two-word value it sets S_f0 = T_f0 + q, adds the carry to S_f1, subtracts T from X with _FP_FRAC_DEC_2 and adds q to R_f0; then shifts X left by one and halves q. Finally, if X_f0 | X_f1 is nonzero it sets the _FP_WORK_ROUND bit of R_f0 if S < X (two-word compare) and always sets _FP_WORK_STICKY in R_f0. q, X, S, T and R are modified; the second loop ends only if q reaches exactly _FP_WORK_ROUND.
note: Macro; contract named identifiers that are not in the file and is dropped. Rewritten from the body.

name: _FP_FRAC_ASSEMBLE_2
prose: Function-like macro, an expression of type void. If rsize <= _FP_W_TYPE_SIZE it assigns r = X_f0; otherwise it assigns r = X_f1, shifts r left by _FP_W_TYPE_SIZE, and adds X_f0, so r gets (X_f1 << word) + X_f0 in r's own type (r must be wider than one word for that to hold). It has no value, only assigns r, and the header comment says no shifting or overflow handling is done.
note: Macro; contract dropped.

name: _FP_FRAC_DISASSEMBLE_2
prose: Function-like macro (do { } while (0), no value). It assigns X_f0 = r (converted to the word type) and X_f1 = 0 if rsize <= _FP_W_TYPE_SIZE, otherwise X_f1 = r >> _FP_W_TYPE_SIZE. r is evaluated more than once.
note: Macro; contract dropped.

name: _FP_FRAC_CONV_1_2
prose: Function-like macro (do { } while (0), no value) converting a two-word source fraction S to a one-word destination fraction D. If S_c != FP_CLS_NAN it applies _FP_FRAC_SRS_2(S, _FP_WFRACBITS_sfs - _FP_WFRACBITS_dfs, _FP_WFRACBITS_sfs), a right shift by the difference in fraction widths that sets a sticky bit for shifted-out bits; if S is a NaN it applies _FP_FRAC_SRL_2 with the same shift count, a plain right shift without sticky. Then it sets D_f = S_f0. The source S is shifted in place.
note: Old prose called the shift 'arithmetic'; it is a sticky right shift (SRS) for non-NaN and a logical right shift (SRL) for NaN. Macro; contract dropped.

name: _FP_FRAC_CONV_2_1
prose: Function-like macro (do { } while (0), no value) converting a one-word source fraction S to a two-word destination D: D_f0 = S_f, D_f1 = 0, then _FP_FRAC_SLL_2(D, _FP_WFRACBITS_dfs - _FP_WFRACBITS_sfs), a left shift by the difference of the fraction widths. S_f is unchanged.
note: Macro; contract dropped.

name: __FP_FRAC_SUB_3
prose: Function-like macro (do { } while (0), no value), compiled only if not already defined (#ifndef __FP_FRAC_SUB_3). It sets r0 = x0 - y0 and _c1 = (r0 > x0); r1 = x1 - y1 and _c2 = (r1 > x1); then r1 -= _c1 and _c2 |= (r1 > _c1); finally r2 = x2 - y2 - _c2. The borrow test in the third step compares the already decremented r1 with _c1 rather than testing whether subtracting _c1 wrapped r1, so it sets _c2 (and subtracts an extra 1 from r2) in cases with no borrow: for example x = (0, 5, 3), y = (0, 0, 1) gives _c1 = 0, r1 = 5, _c2 = (5 > 0) = 1 and r2 = all ones instead of 0. So the macro does not compute the three-word difference modulo 2^(3W) for all inputs; an architecture may provide its own definition.
note: Reviewer right: round 15 pointed at the borrow condition r1 > _c1; confirmed with the counterexample above (compare __FP_FRAC_ADD_3, which uses r1 < _c1 correctly). The old prose claimed the correct modular difference.

name: LM3560_FLASH_BRT_uA_TO_REG
prose: Function-like macro: expands to ((a) < 62500 ? 0 : (((a) - 62500) / 62500)). It yields 0 if a is below 62500, and otherwise the integer-division quotient of (a - 62500) by 62500, i.e. the number of whole steps of 62500 above the minimum. The argument a is evaluated twice and its type decides the arithmetic; there is no upper-limit clamp.
note: Macro; no contract (macro, earlier contracts were rejected for syntax). Old prose assumed a non-negative a; for a below the minimum (including negative a) the result is 0.

name: LM3560_FLASH_TOUT_ms_TO_REG
prose: Function-like macro: expands to ((a) < 32 ? 0 : (((a) - 32) / 32)). It yields 0 if a is below 32, and otherwise the integer-division quotient of (a - 32) by 32, i.e. the number of whole steps of 32 above the minimum. The argument a is evaluated twice and its type decides the arithmetic; there is no upper-limit clamp.
note: Macro; no contract (macro, earlier contracts were rejected for syntax). Old prose assumed a non-negative a; for a below the minimum (including negative a) the result is 0.

name: LM3560_TORCH_BRT_uA_TO_REG
prose: Function-like macro: expands to ((a) < 31250 ? 0 : (((a) - 31250) / 31250)). It yields 0 if a is below 31250, and otherwise the integer-division quotient of (a - 31250) by 31250, i.e. the number of whole steps of 31250 above the minimum. The argument a is evaluated twice and its type decides the arithmetic; there is no upper-limit clamp.
note: Macro; no contract (macro, earlier contracts were rejected for syntax). Old prose assumed a non-negative a; for a below the minimum (including negative a) the result is 0.

name: calipso_exit
prose: The definition in this header is the empty inline stub in the #else branch of CONFIG_NETLABEL: it takes no arguments, does nothing and returns nothing. When CONFIG_NETLABEL is defined the header only declares void calipso_exit(void) and the real function is defined elsewhere, so none of this describes that version.
note: Old prose said no state is changed without naming the config condition; qualified.

name: inet_steal_sock
prose: Calls sk = skb_steal_sock(skb, refcounted, &prefetched), which takes skb->sk away from the skb and sets *refcounted and prefetched; if that gives NULL it returns NULL. If the socket was not prefetched or is not a full socket it returns sk. If sk_protocol is IPPROTO_TCP and the state is not TCP_LISTEN, or IPPROTO_UDP and the state is not TCP_CLOSE, or the protocol is any other, it returns sk. Otherwise it calls inet_lookup_reuseport(net, sk, skb, doff, saddr, sport, daddr, ntohs(dport), ehashfn); if that returns NULL it returns sk, else it executes WARN_ON_ONCE(*refcounted) (it does not itself clear *refcounted; it expects it to be false) and returns the reuseport socket. In this tree neither skb_steal_sock nor inet_lookup_reuseport returns an error pointer. It takes no locks itself.
note: Reviewer mixed: right that the old text said *refcounted is false for reuse_sk (the code only warns if it is true); wrong that skb_steal_sock can return an ERR_PTR (include/net/request_sock.h:94-123 returns NULL or a socket; inet_lookup_reuseport, net/ipv4/inet_hashtables.c, returns NULL or a socket).

name: __inet_lookup_skb
prose: Gets net = skb_dst_dev_net_rcu(skb) and iph = ip_hdr(skb), then sk = inet_steal_sock(net, skb, doff, iph->saddr, sport, iph->daddr, dport, refcounted, inet_ehashfn). If sk is an error pointer it returns NULL; if sk is non-NULL it returns it (whether or not it was prefetched); otherwise it returns __inet_lookup(net, skb, doff, iph->saddr, sport, iph->daddr, dport, inet_iif(skb), sdif, refcounted), the established-then-listener lookup, which can return NULL. *refcounted is whatever inet_steal_sock left for a stolen socket (false when nothing was stolen), and __inet_lookup then sets it true for an established match and false for a listener match or NULL. The caller needs the RCU protection that skb_dst_dev_net_rcu requires.
note: Reviewer right: the old prose said a stolen socket is returned only if prefetched; the code returns any non-NULL non-error stolen socket (include/net/inet_hashtables.h __inet_lookup_skb). Tail of the function was cut in the slice; read from the header.

name: key32_to_tunnel_id
prose: Converts a 32-bit big-endian tunnel key into the 64-bit big-endian tunnel id: on a big-endian build it returns (__force __be64)key, i.e. the numeric value of key zero-extended; on a little-endian build it returns the numeric value (u64)key << 32, so the key sits in the upper 32 bits of the 64-bit value and the low 32 bits are zero. No state is touched.
note: Reviewer mixed. Rounds 1 and 2 objected to earlier wordings; the current text matches scratch-dump lines 1627-1631 (#ifdef __BIG_ENDIAN: (__be64)key, else (u64)key << 32). Round 15 was right that the contract (either result on any host) was too weak; contract removed because endianness cannot be stated in it.

name: __netif_txq_completed_wake
prose: Function-like macro, a GNU statement expression of type int; its arguments (including get_desc, pkts and down_cond) may be evaluated more than once. It first calls netdev_txq_completed_mb(txq, pkts, bytes) unconditionally, which reports the completion to BQL (netdev_tx_completed_queue) when CONFIG_BQL is enabled and otherwise does an smp_mb() if bytes != 0. It then sets _res = -1, and only if pkts is nonzero and get_desc >= start_thrs does it set _res = 1 and, if netif_tx_queue_stopped(txq) and !(down_cond), call netif_tx_wake_queue(txq) and set _res = 0. The value is 0 if the queue was woken, 1 if pkts was nonzero and get_desc reached start_thrs but the queue was not woken (already running or down_cond true), and -1 if pkts is 0 or get_desc < start_thrs.
note: Reviewer right: the old prose said -1 only when start_thrs was not reached; the code also gives -1 when pkts == 0. Macro; contract dropped (it did not type-check).

name: static void cond_react_##name(type curr_state, type event)
prose: Generated by DECLARE_RV_REACTING_HELPERS(name, type) as cond_react_<name>. With CONFIG_RV_REACTORS it returns immediately if rv_reacting_on() is false or rv_<name>.react is NULL; otherwise it calls rv_<name>.react with the format 'rv: monitor %s does not allow event %s on state %s' and the monitor name, the event name from model_get_event_name_<name>(event) and the state name from model_get_state_name_<name>(curr_state). Without CONFIG_RV_REACTORS the generated body is just return, doing nothing. Returns void.
note: Old prose described only the CONFIG_RV_REACTORS variant; the #else variant added.

name: static inline void da_monitor_reset_##name(struct da_monitor *da_mon)
prose: Generated by DECLARE_DA_MON_GENERIC_HELPERS as da_monitor_reset_<name>. It sets da_mon->monitoring to 0 and da_mon->curr_state to model_get_initial_state_<name>(), with plain stores, and returns nothing.
note: Checked against scratch-dump lines 1961-1965.

name: static inline void da_monitor_start_##name(struct da_monitor *da_mon)
prose: Generated by DECLARE_DA_MON_GENERIC_HELPERS as da_monitor_start_<name>. It sets da_mon->curr_state to model_get_initial_state_<name>() and then da_mon->monitoring to 1 with plain stores, and returns nothing.
note: Checked against scratch-dump lines 1973-1977.

name: static inline bool da_monitoring_##name(struct da_monitor *da_mon)
prose: Generated by DECLARE_DA_MON_GENERIC_HELPERS as da_monitoring_<name>. It returns da_mon->monitoring converted to bool and changes nothing.
note: Checked against scratch-dump lines 1982-1985.

name: static inline bool da_monitor_enabled_##name(void)
prose: Generated by DECLARE_DA_MON_GENERIC_HELPERS as da_monitor_enabled_<name>. It returns 0 if rv_monitoring_on() is false, returns 0 if rv_<name>.enabled is false, and returns 1 otherwise. It changes nothing.
note: Checked against scratch-dump lines 1990-2001.

name: static inline bool da_monitor_handling_event_##name(struct da_monitor *da_mon)
prose: Generated by DECLARE_DA_MON_GENERIC_HELPERS as da_monitor_handling_event_<name>. It returns 0 if da_monitor_enabled_<name>() is false, returns 0 if da_monitoring_<name>(da_mon) is false, and returns 1 otherwise. It changes nothing.
note: Checked against scratch-dump lines 2006-2017.

name: da_event_##name(struct da_monitor *da_mon, enum events_##name event)
prose: Generated by DECLARE_DA_MON_MODEL_HANDLER_IMPLICIT as da_event_<name>(da_mon, event), returning bool. It reads da_mon->curr_state with READ_ONCE, then up to MAX_DA_RETRY_RACING_EVENTS times: next_state = model_get_next_state_<name>(curr_state, event). If that is INVALID_STATE it calls cond_react_<name>, calls trace_error_<name> with the state and event names, and returns false without changing the state. Otherwise it tries try_cmpxchg(&da_mon->curr_state, &curr_state, next_state); if that succeeds it calls trace_event_<name> with the old state name, event name, new state name and whether the new state is final, and returns true. If the compare-and-exchange fails, curr_state is refreshed with the current value and the loop retries. After all retries fail it calls trace_rv_retries_error and pr_warn (whose text says the monitor is reset, but no reset is performed here) and returns false.
note: Checked against scratch-dump lines 2031-2058; there is no da_monitor_reset call in the function.

name: da_event_##name(struct da_monitor *da_mon, struct task_struct *tsk, enum events_##name event)
prose: Generated by DECLARE_DA_MON_MODEL_HANDLER_PER_TASK as da_event_<name>(da_mon, tsk, event), returning bool. It does the same as the implicit variant: READ_ONCE of da_mon->curr_state, then up to MAX_DA_RETRY_RACING_EVENTS attempts of next_state = model_get_next_state_<name>(curr_state, event); on INVALID_STATE it calls cond_react_<name> and trace_error_<name>(tsk->pid, state name, event name) and returns false with no state change; on a successful try_cmpxchg of curr_state it calls trace_event_<name>(tsk->pid, old state, event, new state, is-final) and returns true; a failed compare-and-exchange retries with the refreshed state. After all retries fail it calls trace_rv_retries_error and pr_warn (whose text says the monitor is reset, but no reset is performed) and returns false. tsk is used only for tsk->pid in the traces.
note: Checked against scratch-dump lines 2069-2099.

name: static struct da_monitor *da_get_monitor_##name(void)
prose: The instance generated by DECLARE_DA_MON_INIT_GLOBAL as da_get_monitor_<name>: it returns the address of the file-static struct da_monitor da_mon_<name> and changes nothing. (DECLARE_DA_MON_INIT_PER_CPU generates a function of the same name that returns this_cpu_ptr instead.)
note: Checked against scratch-dump lines 2109-2117.

name: static struct da_monitor *da_get_monitor_##name(void)
prose: The instance generated by DECLARE_DA_MON_INIT_PER_CPU as da_get_monitor_<name>: it returns this_cpu_ptr(&da_mon_<name>), the calling CPU's struct da_monitor, and changes nothing. this_cpu_ptr must be used in a context where the CPU cannot change (for example with preemption disabled). (DECLARE_DA_MON_INIT_GLOBAL generates a function of the same name that returns the single global monitor.)
note: Checked against scratch-dump lines 2157-2160.

name: static void da_monitor_reset_all_##name(void)
prose: The instance generated by DECLARE_DA_MON_INIT_GLOBAL as da_monitor_reset_all_<name>: it calls da_monitor_reset_<name>(da_get_monitor_<name>()) on the single global monitor, which sets its monitoring flag to 0 and its state to the initial state. Returns nothing.
note: Checked against scratch-dump lines 2122-2125.

name: static void da_monitor_reset_all_##name(void)
prose: The instance generated by DECLARE_DA_MON_INIT_PER_CPU as da_monitor_reset_all_<name>: for each CPU in cpu_online_mask it calls da_monitor_reset_<name>() on that CPU's monitor (per_cpu_ptr), setting its monitoring flag to 0 and its state to the initial state. CPUs that are not online are not touched. Returns nothing.
note: Checked against scratch-dump lines 2165-2173.

name: static inline int da_monitor_init_##name(void)
prose: Generated by DECLARE_DA_MON_INIT_GLOBAL and DECLARE_DA_MON_INIT_PER_CPU as da_monitor_init_<name>. In both versions it calls da_monitor_reset_all_<name>() and returns 0.
note: Old prose said 'it never fails'; true of these bodies (the only return is 0), reworded to say what it returns.

name: static inline void da_monitor_destroy_##name(void)
prose: Generated by DECLARE_DA_MON_INIT_GLOBAL and DECLARE_DA_MON_INIT_PER_CPU as da_monitor_destroy_<name>. In both versions the body is just return: it does nothing and returns nothing.
note: Checked against scratch-dump lines 2139-2142 and 2187-2190.
